haiku-low.q1: 401 Unauthorized. Redis is not called, so no budget is used.
haiku-low.q2: Standard: 100 requests per minute total, since all keys share the customer's counter. Enterprise: NOT STATED (open question).
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After. The backend never sees the request.
haiku-low.q4: No. The count is not incremented when a request is rejected.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. Counting happens inside check_and_incr before forwarding, so the request still counts.
haiku-low.q6: Fail open: one attempt, 50 ms timeout, no retry. The request is forwarded uncounted, with no X-RateLimit headers, and a metric is emitted.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests/minute. Enterprise: NOT STATED (Product has not decided the limit).
haiku-low.q8: One shared Redis holds counters keyed rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Redis deletes each key when its 120 s TTL expires.
haiku-low.q9: Windows are fixed one-minute UTC-aligned periods. Each new minute uses a new key starting at 0, so the count resets.
haiku-low.q10: check_and_incr is a single Lua script that Redis runs atomically, one script at a time, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: Seconds left until the current minute ends, rounded up, minimum 1.
haiku-low.q12: No retry is made. The client gets the response with no X-RateLimit headers, since the count is unknown.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. Redis is not called, so no counter is affected and no budget is used.
sonnet.q2: Counters are keyed by customer ID, not API key, so all three keys share one budget: the customer's plan limit per minute in total (Standard 100/min; Enterprise limit not decided).
sonnet.q3: A 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. The backend never sees the request.
sonnet.q4: No. The count is not incremented when rejected.
sonnet.q5: Yes. Counting happens in check_and_incr before forwarding, so it counts even if the backend returns 500.
sonnet.q6: The gateway emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric and forwards the request to the backend (fail open, not counted). The response has no X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard = 100 requests/minute. Enterprise = NOT STATED (open question; Product has not decided).
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis used by all 6 gateway instances, with key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Redis deletes each counter key when its 120 s TTL expires; nothing else removes them.
sonnet.q9: Windows are fixed one-minute periods aligned to the UTC clock minute (per Redis's clock). Each new minute uses a new key, so the count starts again at 0.
sonnet.q10: check_and_incr is a single Lua script that Redis runs atomically, one script at a time, so two instances can never both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Retry-After = seconds left until the current minute is over, rounded up, minimum 1.
sonnet.q12: No retry: one attempt with a 50 ms timeout. The client gets no rate-limit information (no X-RateLimit headers) because the count is unknown.
